channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: OpenAI Deploys Continuous Security Testing on Pando Git
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a new Git backend, using Codex agents over 10 weeks while maintaining engineering work. The system now runs continuous red-team testing against Git and Pando to secure its AI-driven development workload. This represents an industry shift toward automated security validation in DevOps pipelines.

item.title: Cisco Email Gateway Vulnerability Enables Root RCE
item.description: A SQL injection flaw in Cisco AsyncOS email parsing lets unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary OS commands with root privileges on Secure Email Gateway devices. The flaw arises from insufficient email content validation, allowing crafted SQL statements to trigger command execution. Cisco released patches; no workarounds exist, so deploy the update immediately and monitor for unauthorized command execution.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Abuse Internal AI Tool and Fake Job Interviews in $6.34 Billion Binance Heist
item.description: North Korean hackers used a fake job interview, a poisoned coding task, and a hijacked internal AI tool to reach Binance’s wallet systems. The FBI says the North Korean group it calls “TraderTraitor” stole more than $6 billion in digital assets on 29 October 2026.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Kernel Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel security update for RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support, addressing several high‑impact kernel flaws. The update is rated Critical by Product Security, with CVSS scores linked to CVE references, implying potential unauthenticated remote code execution. Administrators should apply the patch promptly to mitigate exploitation risks and preserve system integrity.

item.title: mSecure Urges Users to Secure Stored Login Data
item.description: mSeven Software detected suspicious activity affecting mSecure password manager customers. The company urged current and former users to immediately protect stored passwords, two-factor authentication methods, and passkeys. This warning extends beyond routine password reset notices. Organizations should enforce credential rotation and review account access logs for unauthorized sessions.

item.title: Barracuda Vulnerabilities Chain to Root Access
item.description: Barracuda disclosed two vulnerabilities that, when chained, allow an attacker to bypass authorization and gain root on affected devices. The pre‑authentication bypass and command injection flaws, identified as CVE‑2026‑116606 with a CVSS score of 9.3, enable unauthenticated remote code execution. Apply the vendor‑issued patch immediately; no workarounds exist, and monitor for privilege escalation anomalies.

item.title: Hackers Use AI Agents to Launch 3AM Ransomware Attacks Against UK School Networks
item.description: A ransomware affiliate has hit a group of UK schools with a mix of human control and AI-style automation. The attackers used built-in Windows tools, stolen backup passwords and fake admin accounts to spread across the school network, then encrypted about 37 machines.

item.title: Hackers Raise Supermarket Freezers to 50°C
item.description: Hackers targeted supermarket refrigeration systems in at least ten European countries, manipulating temperature controls to raise freezers to 50°C. The attack forced retailers to remove chilled and frozen goods, exposing the vulnerability of connected HVAC equipment and threatening the food supply chain. Operators should isolate affected systems, apply vendor firmware updates, and enforce stricter access controls to prevent further sabotage.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Kernel Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel security update for RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support, addressing CVE-2026-64832. The vulnerability is rated Important by Product Security, with a CVSS score linked to the CVE reference, indicating potential kernel exploitation. Administrators should apply the patch promptly to mitigate the risk and maintain kernel integrity.

item.title: cPGuard Update Channel Compromised, Backdoor Deployed
item.description: An attacker hijacked the cPGuard update channel on November 2, delivering a malicious script that installed a backdoor on customers’ Linux servers. The backdoor harvested password hashes and other sensitive files, and the attacker subsequently exfiltrated portions of the collected data. cPGuard released version 5.88.25 and later with a patched update mechanism; users should upgrade immediately and verify update integrity.

item.title: Barracuda Issues Root‑Privilege Vulnerability Alerts
item.description: Barracuda Networks warned that two undisclosed vulnerabilities in its device firmware can grant attackers root‑level command execution. The flaws allow local or remote attackers to bypass authentication and run arbitrary code with full system privileges. Barracuda released firmware patches for affected devices; administrators should apply the updates and enforce strict access controls.

item.title: USN-8973-1: libmspack vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that libmspack did not properly initialize pointers when handling errors while reading KWAJ archive headers. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause libmspack to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel‑rt Critical Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a critical kernel‑rt update for Enterprise Linux 9.2 SAP, addressing vulnerabilities that could allow privilege escalation. The update mitigates CVE‑2026‑43871, a flaw with a CVSS score that Red Hat rates as critical, though no active exploitation is reported. Deploy the patch immediately; no workarounds are available, and monitor for kernel‑level anomalies.

item.title: Frontline Education Breach Exposes 1.3 Million Records
item.description: Hackers exploited a flaw in third‑party software used by Frontline Education, compromising personal data of staff and students. The vulnerability enabled unauthorized extraction of names, addresses, and academic details, affecting more than 1.3 million individuals. Frontline Education has notified affected parties, coordinated with the vendor to patch the flaw, and urged MFA enforcement.

item.title: Videostrong Deploys Backdoor in 1.3 Million Android TV Boxes
item.description: Videostrong embedded a hidden backdoor in more than 1.3 million Android set‑top boxes, creating a covert botnet. The flaw allowed remote command execution without authentication, enabling attackers to issue arbitrary instructions and exfiltrate data from compromised devices. Affected manufacturers should release firmware updates to remove the backdoor, and security teams must monitor device traffic for anomalous outbound connections.

item.title: USN-8970-1: GVfs vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-84267) It was discovered that GVfs did not properly validate the size of replies from an AFP server. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-84269) It was discovered that GVfs did not properly validate the size of data returned by an MTP device.

item.title: Novee puts forgotten internet-facing assets through penetration testing
item.description: Novee’s External Surface Testing is a new capability in its AI penetration testing platform that helps security teams discover internet-facing assets and validate exploitable vulnerabilities. It tests newly disclosed CVEs and findings imported from third-party external attack surface management (EASM) tools. “Attackers don’t limit themselves to the applications you’re already testing.

item.title: Cloudflare Launches Zero Wire for Vulnerability Triage
item.description: Cloudflare introduced Zero Wire, a platform that aggregates plain‑language briefings with real‑time attack telemetry to aid security teams. Zero Wire enables faster triage of critical CVEs by providing remediation steps and contextual threat data alongside Cloudflare Radar insights. Security teams can integrate Zero Wire into their workflow to prioritize patches and adjust defenses based on up‑to‑date telemetry.

item.title: 3AM Ransomware Hits UK School Estate
item.description: A 3AM ransomware affiliate targeted a UK school estate, encrypting about 37 of nearly 50 machines accessed from an unmanaged host. The attack leveraged an unpatched remote execution flaw in the host’s management software, enabling credential theft and lateral movement across the network. Administrators should apply the vendor’s latest patch, enforce least‑privilege access, and isolate backups to prevent further spread.

item.title: 3AM Affiliate Uses AI‑Like Loops in School Attack
item.description: Investigators found a 3AM ransomware affiliate used an AI‑like model to generate and refine attack commands during a breach of a European school network. The model’s iterative loops enabled real‑time payload adaptation, yet researchers found no evidence of full automation. Teams should monitor command logs, enforce privilege limits, and apply current ransomware defenses.

item.title: Assured Launches CleanRoom SCAN for Backup Hygiene
item.description: Assured Data Protection introduced CleanRoom SCAN, a managed service that independently scans isolated backup copies using multiple security engines. The service detects malware and indicators of compromise before restoration, reducing the risk of reinfecting production environments during recovery. Organizations should adopt CleanRoom SCAN to validate backup integrity and apply remediation before deploying recovered data.

item.title: ARTEX AI Automates Enterprise Attacks at Machine Speed
item.description: Attackers employ the ARTEX AI framework to accelerate credential‑based attacks, enabling rapid cloud privilege escalation, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Recent campaigns demonstrate the framework’s ability to automate complex intrusion stages in minutes, raising concerns for organizations relying on traditional detection methods. Defenders should adopt AI‑aware monitoring, enforce strict credential hygiene, and update detection rules to counter ARTEX‑driven attacks.

item.title: Russia-Linked Spies Target Ukrainian War Crimes Data
item.description: Russian‑linked actors deployed simple malware to exfiltrate sensitive documents and login credentials from Ukrainian war‑crimes investigators and military aid entities. The attacks relied on credential theft rather than a zero‑day flaw, limiting impact to compromised accounts and confidential records. Teams should enforce MFA, monitor anomalous logins, and apply vendor patches to prevent further exfiltration.

item.title: Police Seize 100+ Servers in European Investment Fraud Crackdown
item.description: European authorities conducted a coordinated operation that seized more than 100 servers used by a fraudulent investment network targeting online trading platform users. The sites prevented victims from withdrawing profits, defrauding them of over four million euros and exposing sensitive financial data. Police arrested seven suspects and dismantled the infrastructure, ending the scam and protecting market integrity.

item.title: Renault Car’s 15-Year-Old Linux Navigation Software Hacked to Execute Arbitrary Root Commands
item.description: A security researcher has found a way to run any command with root rights on the navigation unit in a 2014 Renault Latitude. The unit is a TomTom Carminat LIVE head unit that runs a custom system built on Linux 2.6.28.10.

item.title: Wiz Green Agent Speeds Critical Risk Resolution
item.description: Wiz Green Agent, an agentic remediation tool, deployed by Fireblocks, Rogo, and project44 to address cross-team blockers in critical risk resolution. The platform automates remediation workflows, reducing manual coordination overhead and accelerating mean-time-to-remediate for high-severity findings. Organizations can adopt similar agentic approaches to streamline vulnerability management and eliminate operational bottlenecks.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Critical Kernel Patch for CVE‑2026‑64832
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for RHEL 10.0 Extended Update Support to address CVE‑2026‑64832, a critical security flaw. The vulnerability is a kernel‑level bug that could allow unauthenticated attackers to gain elevated privileges, with a CVSS base score indicating critical impact. Red Hat has released the patch; administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: AI Agents Accelerate China‑Linked Espionage Attacks
item.description: A China‑linked espionage group deployed AI agents to compromise over 200 organizations in 11 days, according to CrowdStrike. The attackers leveraged large language models to autonomously select commands, enabling rapid, low‑interaction phishing and credential‑stealing campaigns across diverse sectors. Security teams should enforce multi‑factor authentication, monitor for anomalous credential usage, and deploy AI‑driven threat detection to mitigate automated attack vectors.

item.title: Microsoft Study Links 78% of Exploits to System Takeover
item.description: Microsoft’s research identifies that 78% of real-world exploits target vulnerabilities enabling system takeover or privilege escalation. The study references CVE-2026-112816, a flaw that permits remote code execution without authentication, underscoring the prevalence of high‑impact weaknesses in widely deployed software. Security teams should review patch status for CVE-2026-112816 and prioritize updates to mitigate similar privilege‑escalation vectors.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Critical Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical kernel update for Enterprise Linux 9.2 SAP, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable privilege escalation. The patch addresses CVE‑2026‑43871, a flaw rated critical by Red Hat, with no known active exploitation. Apply the update immediately; no workarounds exist, and monitor kernel activity for anomalies in all environments.

item.title: Android November 2026 Update Fixes 200+ Vulnerabilities
item.description: Android’s November 2026 update patches over 200 flaws, including a critical framework bug that allows remote code execution without user interaction. The bug exploits unchecked permission handling, giving attackers system‑level code execution, a high‑severity vulnerability that can compromise device integrity. Install the update immediately and verify framework component patching to block exploitation.

item.title: Node-RED Authentication Flaw (CVE-2026-58115) Used to Deploy Linux Bots and Backdoors
item.description: Attackers exploited Node‑RED’s authentication flaw (CVE‑2026‑58115) to gain remote code execution on unprotected industrial control servers. The flaw allowed attackers to deploy Linux bots and webshells, enabling arbitrary command execution and persistent backdoors. Node‑RED released a patch; users must update immediately and restrict flow editor access to mitigate the threat.

item.title: Leakers$ Hijack Billboard Software to Display Porn
item.description: The hacking group Leakers$ gained unauthorized access to remote management software controlling public billboards and used it to display pornographic content. The compromise exploited weak authentication and exposed the billboard control interface, allowing attackers to modify display payloads without detection. Security teams should enforce multi-factor authentication, update firmware, and monitor control traffic to prevent similar incidents.

item.title: AI Discovers Vulnerabilities in Legal Systems
item.description: The article argues that advanced AI can identify logical flaws in legal texts, treating statutes as code susceptible to exploitation. These vulnerabilities arise from ambiguous language or inconsistent provisions, allowing AI‑driven analysis to surface potential loopholes that courts may overlook. The piece calls for legal scholars to adopt formal verification techniques and for lawmakers to review statutes for machine‑readable consistency.

item.title: Subnet Solutions PowerSYSTEM Center
item.description: The following versions of Subnet Solutions PowerSYSTEM Center are affected: PowerSYSTEM Center 2020 PowerSYSTEM Center 2024 >=6.0.x| PowerSYSTEM Center 2026 >=7.0.x| CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 9 Subnet Solutions PowerSYSTEM Center 2 Vulnerabilities Incorrect Authorization, Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Canada Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-63017 Incorrect authorization in PowerSYSTEM Center allows a low-privileged, authenticated user to access resources normally limited to administrators.

item.title: Revolve Card Data Stolen, 1.5 Million Affected
item.description: Revolve reported that attackers accessed and exfiltrated stored card details from its payment platform, potentially compromising up to 1.5 million users. The breach involved credential theft and data‑stealing malware, but no evidence of active exploitation of a zero‑day vulnerability was disclosed. Users should monitor statements, change passwords, and enable two‑factor authentication, while Revolve has issued a patch and security advisory.

item.title: Red Hat Patches Kernel TCP RCE CVE‑2026‑98432
item.description: Red Hat released kernel patches for RHEL 8, 9, and 10 to fix CVE‑2026‑98432, a use‑after‑free flaw in the IPv4 TCP code. The flaw enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code with a CVSS score of 9.8, posing a critical threat. Administrators should apply the update immediately; Ubuntu’s fixes remain in the testing channel pending a stable release.

item.title: Exposure Prioritization Framework Explained
item.description: The report explains how organizations prioritize vulnerability remediation, noting that most exposures are treated as urgent despite low exploitation rates. Gartner data shows fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are actually exploited, yet teams focus on low‑risk exposures, leaving higher‑risk ones unaddressed. Adopting the four‑element framework aligns remediation effort with true risk, improving resource allocation and reducing breach exposure.

item.title: Kernel Race Condition Exploits Cause DoS CVE‑2022‑1205
item.description: Duoming Zhou identified race conditions in the AX.25 amateur radio protocol within the Linux kernel, creating CVE‑2022‑1205, a use‑after‑free flaw. The vulnerability permits local attackers to trigger a denial‑of‑service crash, potentially compromising system stability. Red Hat and other vendors have released kernel updates correcting the flaw across multiple subsystems; administrators should apply the patch promptly.

item.title: Kernel Clock Driver Null Dereference CVE‑2022‑3114
item.description: Duoming Zhou uncovered race conditions in the AX.25 protocol and a null pointer dereference in the i.MX clock driver, creating CVE‑2022‑1205 and CVE‑2022‑3114, both local use‑after‑free flaws. Each vulnerability allows local attackers to trigger a denial‑of‑service crash, potentially destabilizing affected systems. Kernel updates correcting these flaws across multiple architectures have been released; administrators should apply the patches promptly.

item.title: Linux Kernel Subsystems Vulnerabilities Patching Update
item.description: Linux kernel subsystems like USB gadget drivers and memory management contain flaws that could let attackers compromise a system. Improper device input handling and memory allocation could allow privilege escalation or denial of service. Ubuntu released a kernel update patching all affected subsystems; administrators should apply it promptly to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Linux Kernel Bluetooth Use-After-Free Vulnerabilities Fixed
item.description: A use‑after‑free flaw in the Linux kernel Bluetooth subsystem (CVE‑2021‑3640) allows a local attacker to trigger a denial‑of‑service or potentially execute arbitrary code. Another CVE‑2022‑49058 flaw in the kernel’s file‑system infrastructure also permits local privilege escalation or denial‑of‑service. Ubuntu released kernel updates that patch both vulnerabilities; administrators should apply the latest kernel version immediately to mitigate the risks.

item.title: USN-8967-1: Linux kernel (AWS) vulnerability
item.description: Jürgen Groß discovered that the Xen network backend driver in the Linux kernel did not adequately limit the amount of queued packets when a guest did not process them. An attacker in a guest VM can use this to cause a denial of service (excessive kernel memory consumption) in the network backend domain. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-98432.

item.title: Ubuntu Patches Linux Kernel SCSI NFS Flaws
item.description: Ubuntu released USN-8964-1 patching Linux kernel vulnerabilities in SCSI and NFS subsystems allowing system compromise. The flaws, CVE-2022-49082 and CVE-2025-39730, permit memory corruption or privilege escalation via local or network file share access. Administrators must apply kernel updates via standard Ubuntu channels to mitigate exploitation risk.

item.title: Gorbag Exploits WinRAR Flaw for Data Theft
item.description: Gorbag exploited a WinRAR flaw to deploy simple information‑stealing malware against Ukrainian law enforcement, justice, and defense entities. The vulnerability enabled arbitrary code execution via a crafted archive, but no zero‑day status was confirmed, limiting the attack to a known flaw. Teams should patch WinRAR to the latest release and monitor for suspicious archive extraction.

item.title: Harvard Breach Exposes 851,000 Alumni Accounts
item.description: Hackers accessed Harvard University's Alumni Affairs and Development systems in November 2025, compromising over 850,000 email addresses. The breach exposed personal identifiers and contact data, creating a high‑risk exposure for alumni and potential phishing vectors, with no credential theft reported.

item.title: NCSC Warns AI Accelerates Ransomware on Critical Infrastructure
item.description: The UK National Cyber Security Centre warned that AI is enabling ransomware actors to launch attacks on critical infrastructure more quickly and cheaply. Its 2026 Annual Review recorded 1,831 attack reports, including 337 incidents that required Incident Management Team support. The NCSC urges organizations to adopt AI‑aware defenses, such as threat detection and response playbooks, to mitigate accelerated ransomware risks.

item.title: ARES Platform Automates 66 Red Team Attack Modules
item.description: The open‑core ARES platform provides red teams with 66 active modules to simulate attacks against Active Directory and cloud environments. Modules map to over 60 MITRE ATT&CK techniques, enabling comprehensive testing of identity, credential, and cloud configuration defenses. Developed by Mafifrizi and released on GitHub, the tool is free to use and can be integrated into existing penetration‑testing workflows.

item.title: Adobe Commerce Zero-Day Enables PSK Agent RAT Deployment
item.description: Attackers exploited the StyleSmuggler flaw in Adobe Commerce and Magento to install the PSK Agent RAT on e‑commerce servers via remote code execution. The CVE‑2026‑75650 vulnerability allows persistent command execution, traffic tunneling, and survives server restarts, presenting a high‑severity remote access threat. Adobe has released an out‑of‑band patch; administrators should apply the update immediately and monitor for unauthorized processes.

item.title: Gorbag APT Targets Ukrainian Courts with Self‑Deleting Malware
item.description: The Gorbag APT group, aligned with Russia, has breached Ukrainian court and city council systems since February 2025 via spearphishing attachments delivering a self‑deleting stealer. The malware exfiltrates credentials and sensitive data before erasing its traces, complicating detection and response. Teams should enforce MFA, monitor outbound traffic, and apply the latest patches to mitigate Gorbag’s tactics.
